pivotal_trials.result: Median OS 9.0 vs 6.6 months; HR 0.56 (95% CI: 0.39, 0.81); p=0.0011; median PFS 2.0 vs 1.0 months (by IRC); HR 0.41 (95% CI: 0.28, 0.59); p<0.0001; ORR 0.9% vs 0%

key_safety: Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 49% of TAS-102 vs 10% of placebo patients, with the most common being neutropenia (38% Grade 3-4), anemia (18% Grade 3), thrombocytopenia (5% Grade 3-4), nausea (48% all grades), fatigue (35% all grades), and diarrhea (32% all grades).
target_moa: Trifluridine (FTD) is a thymidine-based nucleoside analogue that incorporates into DNA to inhibit DNA function and cell proliferation; tipiracil (TPI) inhibits thymidine phosphorylase to prevent rapid degradation of FTD, increasing systemic FTD exposure

_meta.indication: LONSURF is indicated for the treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer who have been previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF biological therapy, and if RAS wild-type, an anti-EGFR therapy.

indication_details.population_restrictions: RAS wild-type patients must have also received prior anti-EGFR therapy; no age/other biomarker restrictions specified
indication_details.prior_therapy_required: fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin- and irinotecan-based chemotherapy; an anti-VEGF biological therapy; and if RAS wild-type, an anti-EGFR therapy

supplements.description: Expanded indication to include treatment of "adult patients with metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma previously treated with at least two prior lines of chemotherapy that included a fluoropyrimidine, a platinum, either a taxane or irinotecan, and if appropriate, HER2/neu-targeted therapy" — a new tumor type beyond Lonsurf's original colorectal cancer indication.

Expanded indication to include Lonsurf **in combination with bevacizumab** (in addition to existing single-agent use) for "adult patients with metastatic colorectal cancer previously treated with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin- and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF biological therapy, and if RAS wild-type, an anti-EGFR therapy," based on the SUNLIGHT phase III trial.
